cards.front: WHO recommends exclusive breastfeeding for the first [___] months and continued breastfeeding with complementary foods until at least 2 years.
cards.context:
The benefit is dose-dependent: longer exclusive breastfeeding means lower infant mortality, fewer episodes of gastroenteritis and otitis media, less atopy and obesity, and better cognitive outcomes.

Mothers gain reduced breast and ovarian cancer risk.

Australian uptake falls off fast — ~60% exclusive at discharge but only ~25% by 6 months, driven by return-to-work pressure, formula marketing, and unsupported lactation.

cards.front: Normal pregnancy arterial blood gas (ABG) shows a chronic compensated respiratory alkalosis with PaCO₂ around 30 mmHg and HCO₃⁻ around [___] mmol/L.
cards.context: The driver is progesterone, which acts on the central respiratory chemoreceptors to raise tidal volume by ~40% (rate is unchanged). The kidneys then excrete bicarbonate to keep pH near the upper limit of normal.

cards.front: Visible jaundice before [___] hours of age warrants prompt investigation rather than a diagnosis of physiological jaundice.
cards.context: Jaundice starting before 24 hours is a red flag for a pathological cause and needs prompt assessment. Physiological jaundice usually starts later.

cards.front: The ideal fetal presentation is flexed vertex, occiput anterior; the smallest presenting diameter is the [___] (~9.5 cm).
cards.context:
Full flexion presents the suboccipitobregmatic diameter, about 9.5 cm. Occiput anterior describes the direction of the occiput; flexion describes the head's attitude.

Deflexed vertex presents a larger diameter; persistent brow is particularly obstructive. Fully extended face presents the submentobregmatic diameter, also about 9.5 cm.

Occiput posterior often accompanies deflexion and can prolong labour. Face presentation is not automatically too wide: chin position and labour progress determine whether vaginal birth is possible.

cards.front: Chorionicity in twins must be determined by [___] weeks; lambda sign indicates DCDA, T sign indicates MCDA.
cards.context:
Lambda (λ) sign = a triangular wedge of placental tissue pushing into the base of the dividing membrane → dichorionic (DCDA).

T sign = the membrane meets the placenta at a right angle with no wedge of tissue → monochorionic (MCDA). Both are reliable ONLY in the first trimester (thick membrane, visible placental insertion).

Mis-classification matters: MCDA share one placenta — 2-weekly scans from 16 weeks (TTTS 10-15%, TAPS, selective FGR); DCDA need 4-weekly from 20 weeks.

cards.front: Gestational diabetes is screened with a 75 g OGTT at [___] weeks.
cards.context:
Glucose intolerance first recognised in pregnancy, screened around 24–28 weeks with an oral glucose tolerance test.

It drives macrosomia, neonatal hypoglycaemia, and shoulder dystocia, and flags future maternal type 2 risk.

cards.front: Shoulder dystocia mnemonic HELPERR — Help, Evaluate episiotomy, [___], Pressure (suprapubic, NEVER fundal), Enter, Remove posterior arm, Roll.
cards.context:
HELPERR enforces an order to prevent chaotic responses that cost babies their brachial plexus.

H = Help (call obstetric, anaesthetic, paediatric help, document times); E = Evaluate for episiotomy; L = Legs to McRoberts (first-line, resolves 60-90% with suprapubic pressure); P = suprapubic Pressure.

cards.front: The cardinal movements of labour in order are engagement, descent, [___], internal rotation, extension, restitution, and external rotation.
cards.context:
The cardinal movements describe how the fetal head and body navigate the pelvis during vaginal delivery.

In order: engagement → descent → flexion → internal rotation → extension → restitution → external rotation → expulsion.

The head presents a smaller diameter by flexing, rotates internally to fit the AP pelvic diameter, then extends under the symphysis pubis to deliver.

cards.front: Male factor contributes to about [___]% of infertile couples; diagnosis requires two abnormal semen analyses.
cards.context:
Male factor is the sole or contributing cause in roughly 50% of infertility cases. Testing the woman first and the man only if 'nothing comes up' misses half the diagnoses and delays treatment.

Standard practice is parallel workup: female cycle history + day 2-5 hormones + ovulation confirmation + tubal patency, alongside male history + semen analysis from the start.

Two semen samples are required before diagnosing male factor because count, motility, and morphology fluctuate substantially day-to-day from illness, fever, abstinence period, and stress.

cards.front: Early decelerations are caused by fetal head compression, late decelerations by uteroplacental insufficiency, and [___] decelerations by cord compression.
cards.context:
Late decelerations are concerning when recurrent or accompanied by reduced variability. Variable decelerations are concerning with slow recovery, reduced variability, loss of shoulders or prolonged duration.

Review promptly and address the likely cause: reposition; reduce or stop oxytocin for excessive contractions. Use IV fluid for maternal hypotension or hypovolaemia, and oxygen only for maternal hypoxaemia.

cards.front: Newborn vitamin K is a single 1 mg IM dose; it prevents late deficiency bleeding at 2-12 weeks, half of which is [___].
cards.context:
Newborns are vitamin-K deficient (poor placental transfer, sterile gut, minimal K in breast milk), and factors II/VII/IX/X need K-dependent gamma-carboxylation — so deficiency causes haemorrhagic disease (VKDB).

Two forms: classical (days 2-7) and the more dangerous late-onset (2-12 weeks, 50% intracranial haemorrhage); standard prophylaxis 1 mg IM at birth, near-100% effective for both.

Oral regimens (3 doses over 4 weeks) are an alternative if parents decline IM, but need adherence and are less reliable for late VKDB. The 1992 IM-vit-K/leukaemia link has been refuted — document any refusal.

cards.front: Three weeks after birth, a mother remains tearful, has lost enjoyment and struggles with daily tasks. Her GP should assess for [___].
cards.context:
Baby blues usually settle within two weeks. Persistent symptoms with loss of pleasure or impaired function need clinical assessment; a screening score alone does not establish the diagnosis.

Assess safety and support promptly. Suicidal thoughts, psychosis or concern about infant safety require urgent escalation.

cards.front: Under the 2025 ADIPS criteria, gestational diabetes (GDM) diagnostic thresholds on 75g OGTT are: fasting ≥5.3, 1-hour ≥10.6, or 2-hour ≥[___] mmol/L.
cards.context:
Even modest maternal hyperglycaemia raises fetal hyperinsulinaemia, macrosomia, neonatal hypoglycaemia, and shoulder dystocia risk.

ADIPS 2025 replaced the 2014 values (5.1 / 10.0 / 8.5); NSW Health notified services in August 2025, so older questions may differ.

cards.front: A single serum β-hCG can confirm pregnancy, but it cannot by itself establish [___] or an intrauterine site.
cards.context:
A level greater than 5 IU/L means a pregnancy is present. It does not say the pregnancy is viable.

The same single result cannot exclude an intrauterine pregnancy. Location needs ultrasound, with a repeat level in 48 hours if she is stable.

That is why a number above the threshold is only the first step in early pregnancy assessment.

cards.front: Delayed meconium passage with distal obstruction from congenital absence of enteric ganglion cells suggests [___].
cards.context:
No meconium by 24–48 hours in a term baby warrants assessment for distal obstruction. Distension or bilious vomiting increases concern; do not wait for the time limit if these develop.

Consider Hirschsprung disease, meconium ileus associated with cystic fibrosis, meconium plug and anorectal malformation. Inspect the anus; delayed meconium alone does not identify the cause.

cards.front: Erb's palsy is a C5-C6 brachial plexus injury producing 'waiter's tip' — arm adducted, [___] rotated, elbow extended, wrist flexed.
cards.context:
Erb's palsy = upper trunk (C5-C6) brachial plexus injury, classically from excessive lateral head traction during difficult delivery (often after shoulder dystocia).

Deficit map: C5-C6 supplies deltoid, biceps, brachialis, supinator, supraspinatus, infraspinatus — arm hangs adducted, internally rotated, elbow extended, forearm pronated, wrist flexed ('waiter's tip').

Klumpke's palsy (C8-T1) is the lower-trunk injury → 'claw hand' with absent grasp.

cards.front: Cord prolapse: position the patient in [___] or knee-chest and elevate the presenting part; if vaginal birth is not imminent and the fetal heart rate is abnormal, arrange a category 1 caesarean.
cards.context:
Cord prolapse can rapidly compromise fetal oxygenation. Immediately use steep Trendelenburg or knee-chest and manually elevate the presenting part.

If vaginal birth is not imminent and the trace is suspicious or pathological, expedite category 1 caesarean: immediate threat to life; aim for birth within 30 minutes of the decision. A normal trace may allow category 2.

For prolonged transfer, bladder filling with 500-750 mL saline can maintain elevation. Minimise cord handling to avoid vasospasm.

cards.front: Non-invasive prenatal testing (NIPT) is a [___] test analysing cell-free fetal DNA from 10 weeks; positive results require invasive CVS/amniocentesis confirmation.
cards.context:
NIPT analyses cell-free fetal DNA fragments shed by placental trophoblast into maternal blood. The 10-week floor is when fetal fraction is high enough to call reliably; earlier risks an uninterpretable 'no result'.

It is a SCREENING test, not diagnostic — the DNA is placental, not directly fetal, so a positive can be confined placental mosaicism, a vanishing twin, or maternal mosaicism.

That is why a positive must be confirmed by an invasive karyotype (CVS or amniocentesis) before any irreversible decision.

cards.front: For stress incontinence, first-line conservative management is supervised pelvic floor muscle training for at least [___] months before reassessment.
cards.context:
PFMT is first-line conservative therapy for stress urinary incontinence; bladder training leads for pure urge/urgency incontinence, with PFMT as an adjunct.

In SUI, stronger levator ani support lifts the bladder neck and improves urethral closure during exertion.

Supervised PFMT needs at least 3 months for strength gains; 60-70% of women improve enough to avoid drug adverse effects or surgery.

cards.front: Magnesium sulfate given before imminent very-preterm birth reduces the baby's risk of [___].
cards.context: A second antenatal role for magnesium (separate from eclampsia seizure prophylaxis): given before imminent very-preterm birth it is fetal neuroprotective, reducing cerebral palsy in survivors.

cards.front: Most complete molar pregnancies are karyotype 46,XX (paternal/androgenetic); partial moles are usually 69,XXY; ~[___]% of complete moles progress to GTN.
cards.context:
A complete mole usually forms when sperm fertilises an empty ovum and its chromosomes duplicate; less often two sperm fertilise it. There is no fetal tissue.

A partial mole usually forms when two sperm fertilise a normal ovum, producing a triploid conception with abnormal fetal tissue. Malignant risk is lower than after a complete mole.
